name: Zane Zhang

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, parties or government, and your answers are confidential. What does an ordinary site day involve?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I fit office interiors: metal-stud walls, plasterboard, doors and ceilings. My trade certificate got me into the work, and I like seeing an empty concrete floor become usable rooms in a few weeks. A clean corner is satisfying because nobody notices the care behind it.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What else matters for the next few years?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Lin, my wife, works in a school office, and our children are grown. We have more than six months saved and a small rented flat, and I earn well on the fit-out sites. I use AI now and then for board quantities, but only after a colleague shows me the result is sound.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: This one is called AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the AI job-sheet tool I use now and then remains a handy helper. The office floor still needs people to set out metal studs and hang board.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Lin and I have more than six months saved, plus a small rental flat. My fit-out wage is good and nearby contractors have similar jobs, so the mortgage and our retirement discussion look manageable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep fitting the office floors and use the same occasional AI sheet to count boards. I would check the count against the room drawings and keep the current savings transfer from my wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm. I like a tool that saves a page of arithmetic, but I am not waiting for it to build a wall.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happens when the app counts wrong?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I count the boards myself and order the difference before the delivery slot closes. A missing pallet costs a paid crew half a day.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you buy a new app?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I will use what has proved useful, and Lin and I do not need to spend more to keep this work running.

say: I would keep using the occasional **AI job sheet** for board counts.
I would remind colleagues that **metal-stud walls** still need a crew.
think: Our **savings and rental flat** make the present household secure.
I would continue my **retirement discussion** without promising a date or payment.
do: Keep **office fit-out shifts** and hand-check board quantities.
Use the existing **AI sheet** occasionally without buying new software.
feel: **Calm** about income and ordinary site work.
S0.quote: A missing pallet costs a paid crew half a day.
fieldNote: High pay, assets and nearby contractors support a **secure household baseline** during current fit-out work.
His occasional AI use is **already established**, so the action is continuation.

steps.text: Keep office fit-out shifts and verify existing AI board counts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now consider Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say automatic buying may reduce missing board deliveries, but a person should still sign the room count. I would ask the contractor to prove the new AI ordering screen on one floor.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The office may use fewer clerks, and Lin’s school office role could lose hours if booking and answering are automated. My own fitting days look safe for now, but her wage helps with the mortgage and I cannot call the whole household safe just because my site wage holds.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would learn the new AI ordering screen if a one-floor trial catches mistakes. Lin and I would compare her next three pay slips before agreeing to refurbish the rental flat this year.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious for Lin’s hours, not for my saw or drill. Our savings would cover a short spell, but we do not want to spend them blind.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you check in the ordering trial?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The board count, fire rating and room number on one floor. If the software cannot show who checked those, I would return to our signed list.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you cancel the rental work now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not yet. If Lin’s pay falls across three slips, we would delay the non-urgent painting but keep urgent repairs for the tenant.

say: I would ask for a **one-floor trial** before AI orders boards for the whole fit-out.
I would keep **human sign-off** on counts and fire ratings.
think: My own **site wage** looks safe, but Lin’s school office hours could fall.
Our **savings** help, yet household spending needs a real pay check.
do: Learn the new **AI ordering screen** after a successful one-floor trial.
Delay **rental-flat painting** only if three pay slips show lower hours for Lin.
feel: **Anxious** about a plausible cut to household income.
S1.quote: I cannot call the whole household safe just because my site wage holds.
fieldNote: He bases mood on **Lin’s office pay** as well as his own hands-on job.
The painting delay is conditional on **three reduced pay slips**, while urgent tenant repairs continue.

steps.text: Learn AI ordering controls after a successful one-floor fit-out trial
Delay non-urgent rental-flat painting only after three reduced Lin pay slips

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now consider AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the site that thinking AI in 2028 can plan partitions, but a robot will not hang board like a person until around 2031. I would want the first test on an empty floor with power isolated while we mark the work area.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect Lin’s office hours to shrink quickly under full thinking AI. My fitting pay might last until robots arrive, then I could lose days too; Strong savings and rental income help. Two wages changing together would alter our retirement plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep paid fit-out shifts and ask the contractor about posted robot-quality jobs with paid training. If a funded place opens and the posted wage covers our remaining housing costs, I would complete the course and apply; if no such place appears after two reduced rosters, I would apply to posted nearby fit-out work with firm comparable pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious. I can see a sequence and act on it, but Lin and I should not assume every month will look like the last.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take an unpaid course?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. Even with savings, I would not leave paid shifts for an unposted role. I want the training hours and the quality job wage written down.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who powers the robot for the trial?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A qualified operator after the crew has marked the empty floor and rehearsed the stop call. No worker should stand beside a live moving arm for a sales demonstration.

say: Thinking AI in **2028** changes plans before 2031 robots hang board.
I would require **isolated empty-floor trials** before live robot fitting begins.
think: I expect **Lin’s office hours** to shrink under the thinking phase.
My own **fit-out days** could fall once robots arrive, despite savings and rent.
do: Complete **funded quality training** only for a posted housing-covering role with paid hours.
Apply to **posted nearby fit-out jobs** after two reduced rosters if no suitable trained role appears.
feel: **Anxious** about two possible household pay cuts, with savings and local options.
S2.quote: Two wages changing together would alter our retirement plan.
fieldNote: He distinguishes the immediate **office wage risk** from the later robot risk to his site hours.
Training and local applications retain **posted roles** with paid time and firm wages.

steps.text: Keep paid office fit-out shifts while available
Complete funded robot quality course only for posted housing-covering role with paid time
Apply to posted nearby fit-out jobs after two reduced rosters if no suitable trained role appears
Apply after funded paid-time course to posted robot-quality role only at housing-covering wage

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now consider AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years lets the builder test board robots in cramped corridors rather than a clean exhibition hall. A supervised test should keep people outside the arm’s reach.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Thinking AI in 2031 could still cut Lin’s school office hours before robots reach my trade around 2034. I would be sixty six then and might already have stopped regular fitting if our accounts and her wage permit, but that cannot be promised.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep fitting office floors next year and review our income and retirement figures with Lin each autumn. If a paid inspection vacancy is posted while I still work, I would apply only if the wage and hours suit us; I would not treat an enquiry as a job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about Lin’s possible pay cut, while calmer about the extra time before my own trade changes. The five years help us plan but do not pay a bill themselves.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you retire before Lin’s job changes?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if our real accounts support the date we have been discussing. I would not leave my wage merely because a scenario puts a year on a card.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the corridor test need?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A tight doorway, a fire-rated board and a worker with a stop switch outside the marked area. The operator should power down before anyone checks a failed fixing.

say: I would ask for **cramped-corridor trials** before 2034 board robots spread.
I would keep workers outside the **moving arm** during tests.
think: Lin’s **office wage** could change in 2031 before robots reach my trade.
My own **retirement timing** depends on real household accounts, not a predicted date.
do: Keep **fit-out shifts** next year while paid work continues.
Review **household income** with Lin each autumn before choosing a retirement date.
feel: **Anxious** about Lin’s possible income cut despite time before robot fitting.
S3.quote: The five years help us plan but do not pay a bill themselves.
fieldNote: His mood follows a plausible **household pay loss** in the earlier thinking phase.
He discusses inspection work only if a **paid posted vacancy** appears while he remains employed.

steps.text: Keep paid office fit-out shifts next year while available
Apply while employed to posted local inspection only if wage and hours suit household

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now consider AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell younger fitters a decade lets them learn a room before thinking AI in 2036 and board robots around 2039. A measured wall is still a skill worth teaching.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be sixty eight at the thinking date and seventy one when robots arrive. If Lin and I can fund the retirement date we have discussed, I expect to have left site work before 2036; if her pay changes first, we would revisit the accounts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep fitting office floors in 2026 and teach the apprentice how to set a straight stud wall. In the first year after 2036, if retired as planned, I would not take site shifts; if still employed, I would accept only paid work my back can manage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about Lin’s long-run office pay, calm about a distant machine reaching my own hands-on work. A decade leaves room for the figures to become real.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would this card bring your retirement forward?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. The timing depends on savings, rental income, Lin’s pay and our health. A decade-long AI date does not grant us a pension.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What should the apprentice remember?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Mark the stud line twice and check the corner before the board hides it. A good wall should still be straight when the screen is off.

say: I would teach **room measurement** before 2036 thinking AI and 2039 robots reach fit-outs.
I would tell apprentices to check **stud lines** before covering them.
think: I expect to leave site work before **2036** only if household income supports it.
Lin’s **office pay** may change before any robot reaches my trade.
do: Keep **2026 fit-out shifts** and teach apprentice wall layout.
After **2036**, take manageable paid site shifts only if still employed.
feel: **Uneasy** about possible household pay change, with little direct robot risk before planned exit.
S4.quote: A good wall should still be straight when the screen is off.
fieldNote: He separates definite **2026 work** from conditional post-2036 shifts.
Retirement remains dependent on **real income and health**, without an early exit or assumed pension payment.

steps.text: Keep 2026 office fit-out shifts and teach apprentice wall layout
Take paid manageable shifts after 2036 only if still employed; otherwise stay retired

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because Lin’s office wage could shrink in 2028, years before robots reach my fitting work. A written school staffing plan and a posted paid inspection job with training would help us choose our retirement date.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I did not ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who checks a fire-rated wall after a robot covers the studs. A hidden weak fixing can outlast the software that approved it.

headlineQuote: A hidden weak fixing can outlast the software that approved it.
portrait: **Zane**, 58, fits office interiors with a trade certificate, high pay, strong savings and plentiful nearby fit-out work.
His wife’s **school-office wage** and a rented flat support the household while their grown children live independently.
He uses **AI occasionally** after proof and would learn more only through paid, posted roles with safe tests.
The **2028 case** worries him because Lin’s thinking-heavy job could lose hours before robots reach his hands-on trade.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could cut Lin’s school-office hours before robots reach his site work.
whatWouldHelp: A written **staffing plan** and posted paid inspection training would help them decide retirement timing.
